questions.answer: In DTR, banishing is the permanent removal of a storage S when it has no evicted dependents, which involves evicting S and removing it entirely from the dependency graph, effectively pinning its dependents as non-rematerializable constants. Banishing can lower runtime overhead but supports less aggressive memory budgets compared to eager eviction.
